Signs You Need To Call a Plumber

At CR Plumbing, we understand that plumbing issues can arise unexpectedly and disrupt your daily routine. Knowing when to call a professional plumber can save you time, money, and stress. Here are some signs that indicate you need to call a plumber in Addison:

Persistent Dripping Faucets: If your faucet continues to drip despite attempts to fix it, it could be a sign of a deeper issue. Persistent dripping not only wastes water but can also indicate problems with your plumbing system.

Slow or Clogged Drains: Slow draining sinks, showers, or tubs can be more than just an inconvenience. These can be signs of a clog or blockage in your plumbing system that requires professional attention to prevent further damage.

Low Water Pressure: Experiencing low water pressure throughout your home can be a sign of a serious problem such as pipe corrosion, hidden leaks, or blockages. A plumber can diagnose and resolve the issue to restore proper water pressure.

Unusual Noises: Strange noises coming from your pipes, such as banging, gurgling, or whistling, can indicate various plumbing problems. These noises should not be ignored, as they can signal issues like water hammer, trapped air, or blockages.

Water Stains and Damp Spots: Noticeable water stains on your walls, ceilings, or floors can indicate a hidden leak. Damp spots and unexplained moisture can lead to mold growth and structural damage if not addressed promptly by a professional.

Sewage Smells: Foul odors coming from your drains or around your property are a clear sign of a sewer line problem. This could be due to a blockage or a break in the sewer line, and immediate professional intervention is necessary.

Frequent Toilet Overflows: If your toilet frequently overflows or gets clogged, it might be more than just a minor inconvenience. This can be a sign of a blockage deeper in your plumbing system that requires professional clearing.

Discolored Water: Brown or yellow water coming from your taps can indicate rust or sediment buildup in your pipes. This can affect your water quality and needs to be addressed by a plumber to ensure your water is safe to use.

Burst Pipes: A burst pipe is an emergency that requires immediate professional attention. This can cause significant water damage and should be handled by a trained plumber to prevent further issues.

High Water Bills: A sudden spike in your water bill without an increase in usage can indicate a hidden leak. A plumber can help locate and fix the leak to save you money and prevent water waste.

article_html:
Homes here tend to be big. That means more bathrooms, longer pipe runs, two or three water heaters and HVAC systems split into zones. When something fails, it’s rarely a quick guess. You want a tech who traces the problem and explains it, not one who swaps parts until it stops.

That’s how our crew works. We’ll tell you what’s wrong, what’s urgent and what can wait. If a $60 part fixes your water heater, that’s what we’ll recommend.

Need a plumber in Southlake today? Call us. Most repairs get finished on the first visit.

Plumbing Repair in Southlake

Water heater problems are our busiest category here. Tank or tankless, we install, repair and replace them. A tank that’s leaking at the base is usually done. One that just lost its heating element or thermostat is usually worth fixing. We’ll tell you which one you’ve got before you spend anything.

Drains and sewer lines come next. We clear clogs with a snake or hydro jet, then send a camera down the line so you can see what caused it. If the camera finds a cracked or collapsed sewer pipe, we’ll go through repair and replacement options, including trenchless methods that save your landscaping.

We also handle leak detection, burst pipes, water line repair, garbage disposals, sump pumps and fixture installs. If it’s an emergency, say so when you call and we’ll move you up.

Heating & AC in Southlake

Southlake summers are hard on air conditioners. Long run times, big square footage, refrigerant leaks and dead capacitors all show up in July. In winter it’s furnaces and heat pumps that won’t start or blow cold air. Our HVAC techs repair, replace and maintain both, and they’ll check the basics first, like filters and thermostat settings, before quoting anything big.

If your system is 15 years old and the repairs keep stacking up, we’ll price a replacement. We won’t push one if a repair makes more sense.

Electrical Work

Flickering lights, warm outlets and breakers that keep tripping are worth a look, not a shrug. Our electricians find the cause, repair wiring, upgrade panels and add circuits for things like EV chargers, hot tubs and generators.

Gas Lines

Smell gas? Get everyone outside and call from there. We locate and repair leaks and pressure test the line before the gas is back on. We also run new lines for ranges, fireplaces, outdoor kitchens and pool heaters.

Water Filtration

Hard water leaves white crust on fixtures and wears out water heaters faster. We test your water first, then recommend a softener or filtration system only if it’ll help. If a simple under-sink filter does the job, that’s what we’ll suggest.
